🔥 गजब का मसाला! सनी पाजी ने देखी Ramayana Part 1 और हॉलीवुड को भी पीछे छोड़ दिया! 😎

🎬 5 नवंबर को सिनेमाघरों में रिलीज हुई Ramayana: Rise of a Legend के पोस्ट-क्रेडिट सीन में सनी देओल Lord Hanuman के रूप में नजर आए हैं।

📸 शनिवार को Instagram पर सनी ने फिल्म का रिव्यू शेयर करते हुए हर हिंदुस्तानी से इसे देखने की अपील की और कहा कि यह फिल्म किसी भी Hollywood film से कम नहीं बल्कि बेहतर है।

⚡ इस पोस्ट-क्रेडिट सीन में Hanuman की एंट्री दमदार म्यूजिक के साथ होती है, जहां वे हवा में गदा लेकर जय श्री राम बोलते नजर आते हैं।

🎵 इस सीन के बैकग्राउंड में Hanuman Chalisa बजती है जिसे Diljit Dosanjh, Sukhwinder Singh, Mohit Chauhan, Kailash Kher और Anirudh Ravichander ने गाया है।

👑 फिल्म में Raghav Juyal मेघनाद के रोल में दिखते हैं, और sequel साल 2028 में आएगा जिसकी नींव हनुमान के आने से मजबूत होती है।

🎥 Nitesh Tiwari निर्देशित इस फिल्म में Ranbir कपूर राम और Sai सीता के रोल में हैं, जबकि Namit Malhotra और Yash इसके प्रोड्यूसर हैं।

👇 क्या आपने यह फिल्म देखी और सनी पाजी का यह अंदाज आपको कैसा लगा? जल्दी से कमेंट में बताओ!

ctx.title: After his post-credit reveal as Lord Hanuman, Sunny Deol reviews Ramayana Part 1 and says it is better than many Hollywood films
ctx.summary: Sunny Deol made a powerful entry as Lord Hanuman and flies with gada in post-credit scene of Ramayana Part 1.
ctx.text:
Ramayana Part 1, also titled Ramayana: Rise of a Legend, released in theatres in November 5. Viewers who have seen the film were treated with one of its biggest reveals in the post-credit scene. It is Sunny Deol who makes an appearance as Lord Hanuman in the closing moments. The actor makes his appearance in a post-credit scene, offering a first glimpse of his character and setting up his role in the second installment.
On Saturday, Sunny took to Instagram to share his review of the film and urged every Hindustani to support it. He said, “I just watched Ramayana. I really, really liked it. I urge each and every Hindustani to watch it. This film is not less than any Hollywood film. But I would say it is better than them. The special effects truly transport the viewer to that time. It is my request to all of you and tell you to go and watch it.”
Meanwhile, the post credit scene opens with a powerful musical backdrop, as Hanuman makes his entry. While his face remains hidden, a wider shot towards the end shows him flying through the air with his gada as he hails Jai Shri Ram. The Hanuman Chalisa, sung by Diljit Dosanjh, Sukhwinder Singh, Mohit Chauhan, Kailash Kher and Anirudh Ravichander, plays in the background, adding to the impact of the moment. The makers have revealed just enough to build curiosity around Sunny's portrayal without giving away his complete look. Before Hanuman's appearance, the film also offers a glimpse of Raghav Juyal as Meghnada, Ravana's eldest son and the crown prince of Lanka.
Hanuman's arrival also marks a significant point in the Ramayana for the sequel which will arrive in 2028. He becomes one of the most important figures in Rama's journey after Ravana abducts Sita. From finding her in Lanka to helping Rama prepare for the war against Ravana, Hanuman plays a crucial role in the events that follow.
Ramayana is directed by Nitesh Tiwari, who co-wrote the screenplay with Shridhar Raghavan. It is produced by Namit Malhotra and Yash. Ranbir plays Ram in the film, Sai plays Sita, and Yash plays Ravana. The film also stars Ravi Dubey as Lakshmana, Rakul Preet Singh as Surpanaka, Arun Govil as Dasharatha, Lara Dutta as Kaikeyi, Shobana as Kaikashi, Kajal Aggarwal as Mandodari, and more.
The first part delves into Ravana’s backstory, setting up the tale till his abduction of Sita after a fight with Jatayu, voiced by Anupam Kher. It also shows Ram’s childhood and upbringing, his marriage to Sita, the circumstances of his 14-year exile, and his vow to bring Sita back from Ravana.
Santanu Das is a Senior Content Producer at Hindustan Times with over 5 years of experience, writing on films, pop culture and film festivals. He has a keen interest in writing about South Asian independent films and has covered several film festivals, including Sundance and CPH: Docx. When not watching films or speaking to celebrities, Santanu can be found reading a book. Some of his favourite films are Aparajito, Ponyo and The Double Life of Veronique. His favourite books include The Corrections, The God of Small Things and A Room of One's Own.

Santanu continues to write passionately about films and celebrity culture. He brings a relatable, as well as critically informed, lens to entertainment and culture for a wide audience.
